scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-AI-FIX.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-response/handling gap that an AI agent can resolve by auto-answering tickets and automatically fixing the underlying bill errors.

H-RULE-CHANGE-ERROR.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August caused systematically wrong bills (e.g., altered estimate-substitution logic), driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: AMI register reads from the vendor (Telemetrix) are failing to deliver or validate correctly via the nightly MDMS export, causing missing/incorrect reads and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter reads from the contracted field service (MeterWorks) are not being delivered or validated correctly via the daily upload, causing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: A field-reading staffing shortage at the contractor is causing missed routes and increased estimated bills, as suggested by SH-FIELD's own account.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-ERROR.statement: A majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) carry an ACTUAL read type, suggesting an error in billing calculation/tariff application on correctly-read meters, independent of missing-read/estimate-substitution causes.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Billing-db shows disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL read type: the majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) carry an ACTUAL meter read, not an ESTIMATED substitution. This means "missing/estimated read" explanations cover only a minority of disputes, and a sizeable share of disputes stem from bills built on actual readings — pointing at billing calculation/tariff/validation issues as well as read-collection failures.

Billing-db's tariff_change_log returned zero records, meaning no tariff changes are recorded in the period covered. This rules out a tariff-rate change as the trigger for the dispute surge, but says nothing about billing-calculation errors unrelated to tariff edits or about import validation rule changes (a separate log).

Route-log reports 88% field route completion against a 95% target for Aug-Sep, with 9200 manual-read accounts in scope. This quantifies a field-route completion shortfall but does not by itself show how many of the 1240 estimated-read disputes it accounts for, nor does it speak to the 1785 actual-read disputes.

CRM data shows dispute-ticket response times (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days) are within the 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, so slow response handling is not demonstrated as a driver of the surge. This undercuts the "slow response" half of CL-01's causal framing and the premise that an AI auto-responder addresses a response-speed gap.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states there has been no tariff change this year. This is an unverified stakeholder claim that aligns in direction with the authoritative tool finding E-02 (zero tariff_change_log records since August), but adds no new authoritative weight on its own.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) claims the contractor has been short three meter readers since July, causing routes to run late and the affected customers to receive estimated bills. This is an unverified, self-interested stakeholder account (SH-FIELD has an incentive to attribute problems to staffing/headcount) consistent in direction with the measured 88% route completion shortfall (E-03), but it does not quantify how many of the 1240 estimated-read disputes this accounts for, and says nothing about the 1785 actual-read disputes.

CRM dispute_volume_monthly shows a baseline of ~600 disputes/month in June-July (610, 590) jumping to roughly double in August-September (1180, 1260). This confirms the magnitude of the surge referenced in the initial request but says nothing about its cause.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 (service contract §4.2) confirms that while the utility may request field route priority changes, they are only executed after Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation — this reaffirms the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint for push_route_update and does not speak to the causal question of what is driving the dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Route-log identifies 14 specific routes falling behind schedule (distinct completion values per route, e.g. 0.7 for R-00), giving route-level granularity behind the aggregate 88% completion figure. It does not by itself quantify how many of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes these lagging routes account for; that cross-reference still requires the pending accounts_estimated_last_cycle billing-db query (W-WI-BILLING-ESTIMATE-XREF).

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: Billing-db's accounts_estimated_last_cycle query (E-10) returns 320 accounts billed on ESTIMATED reads last cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes (sample: AC-20000 on R-00). This supplies the account/route-level data needed to cross-reference against the 14 lagging routes (E-09) for U-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-OVERLA, but the aggregate summary alone does not establish how many of these 320 accounts fall specifically on the 14 lagging routes.

U-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-OVERLA.safe_placeholder: Treat field staffing shortfall as an unquantified contributing factor to the ESTIMATED minority only, not the primary driver.

structural_remedies.description: If the rule-change log confirms a validation-rule change caused calculation errors on ACTUAL-read bills, revert/correct that specific rule in billing-config under SH-BILL's authority and reprocess affected ACTUAL-read accounts.

structural_remedies.description: Escalate under the MeterWorks service contract to restore the three missing readers (since July, E-06) and bring field route completion from 88% back to the 95% target (E-03), reducing ESTIMATED-substitution bills.

structural_remedies.description: Formalize that any confirmed billing errors are remediated only via SH-BILL-authorized manual bill adjustment/credit, explicitly rejecting CL-01's request for an agent that automatically 'fixes' bills, per K-BILLWRITE.
structural_remedies.rationale: This simply enforces the existing K-BILLWRITE authority constraint as the sanctioned remediation channel; no new tooling or approval beyond what already exists is required.; residual gap: This governs how corrections are applied but does not identify or eliminate the underlying error source — it must be paired with remedy 2 (and/or 3) to actually remove the root cause.
